analyst.summary: Apar Industries delivered a record FY26 (revenue +23%, PAT +19%) on the back of its global-leading aluminium conductor franchise, transformer-oil business and cable division, but the quality of that growth is mixed - conductor volumes actually fell in Q3 even as revenue rose on commodity pass-through, consolidated margins are compressing (10%->8%), ROCE is normalizing down from a FY23 super-cycle peak, and the balance sheet is taking on more debt and working capital to fund the ramp. At ~55-57x trailing earnings the stock is priced for sustained hypergrowth the company's own ~15% revenue guidance does not support, and a board-approved Rs.2,500cr fundraise (shareholder vote pending 30-Jul-2026) adds a near-term dilution overhang. We rate the name Hold: a quality franchise, but a rich multiple against real growth-quality and margin questions, with Q1 FY27 results due 24-Jul-2026 as the next test.
